# The Paradox of the Cheap Part: Why Appliance Repair Is Hard

## The Initial Decision

Meet the Hendersons. Their seven-year-old front-loading washing machine, a mid-range model they bought when they moved into their house, has stopped spinning. The drum fills with water, the machine hums, but the clothes come out sopping wet. Mrs. Henderson does a quick search online and discovers the likely culprit: the door lock assembly, a small plastic-and-wire component that tells the machine the door is closed. The part costs $18.95 with free shipping.

The machine itself cost $650 new. A replacement of similar quality today runs $800. On paper, this is an easy decision: spend $18.95 and an afternoon, and save nearly $800. What follows illustrates why the math is never that simple.

## Diagnosis: The First Hurdle
